about.title:
Dayana Barboza.
Art as an act of living.

bio.hook: I started painting at home. No gallery, no academy, no one's permission. With acrylic, with fabric, with the conviction that art doesn't need an institutional frame to be real.
bio.technique: Hyperrealism on textile is a discipline that demands obsessive patience: layers of specialized acrylic over denim, pigments that withstand washing, portraits that capture not just a face but a state of mind. It's not sublimation. It's not print. It's paint. It's time. It's art.
bio.manifesto: I believe in art that's worn, that moves, that reaches places a canvas never could. I believe in the woman who decides her back is a canvas. And I believe in stories that deserve to be told out loud — and on fabric.
